title: finding(components/types): the `ui:calendar` designer offers `mode: 'default'`, which both authoring faces refuse
body:
Surfaced by the dev executing objectui#10304 (PR objectui#10376, `out_of_scope_findings`). Filed by the `domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat, session `session_01877XiBYSaRCk2CU7cMSg3S`. The seat re-measured the two sites below on `origin/main`. ⛔ Not graded: `priority:*` and `type` belong to triage. The seat proposes `domain:spec`, because this is a contract ↔ registration seam.

## Fact (class c: the designer offers a value the contract refuses)

| site | reads |
|:--|:--|
| `packages/components/src/renderers/form/calendar.tsx:42`, the `ui:calendar` registration `inputs` | `{ name: 'mode', type: 'enum', enum: ['default', 'single', 'multiple', 'range'] }` |
| `packages/types/src/form.ts:1169`, `CalendarSchema.mode` | `mode?: 'single' \| 'multiple' \| 'range';` |
| the zod mirror (per the dev's measurement) | `UiCalendarSchema.safeParse({type:'ui:calendar', mode:'default'})` → `invalid_value` at path `mode` |

So an author who picks `default` in the designer stores a document that the mirror refuses and the TS face cannot express.

## Not measured

What react-day-picker 10 does with `mode: 'default'` at runtime. Rule 2 of #7759 ruling 5617465269 says `CalendarSchema` is objectui-own, so the read site is the truth, and the fix direction follows from that measurement:
- If the renderer treats `default` the same as omitting `mode`, drop `'default'` from the designer enum.
- If it has distinct behaviour, admit it on both faces.

## Serial note

This touches the same `ui:calendar` registration and `CalendarSchema` lines as PR objectui#10376 (#10304), so it goes after that PR lands.

Seam: `types:form.ts#CalendarSchema.mode` → `registration:packages/components ui:calendar inputs`
Dedupe words: `ui:calendar mode default` · `calendar inputs enum default` · `calendar mode invalid_value designer`
